    59	def sixRegExtractionEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    60	    SixReg P ιA ιB ≃ ExtractionRegisters P ιA ιB where
    61	  toFun p := (((p.1.1, p.1.2.1), p.1.2.2),
    62	    ((p.2.1, p.2.2.1), p.2.2.2))

    64	    (p.2.1.1, (p.2.1.2, p.2.2)))

   143	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=

   161	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
   162	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/

   229	/-- Conjugation of an operator by a square matrix, as used in the exact

   237	/-- The common error scale for constructing the pulled-apart measurements from

   246	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1458-1605`. -/

   255	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/

   257	  C * (Real.rpow deltaS (1 / 4 : ℝ) + ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))

    75	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:55-62`; paper

  1419	Recall the decoding map of the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}. This map takes in a polynomial $g \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ and returns a string $\coded(g) \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$ consisting of the evaluations of $g$ on the points in the hypercube $\{0,1\}^m$.
  1420	We now use this decoding map to construct a new set of measurement operators out of $\hat{S}$.
  1421	First, we introduce some notation. For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and all degree $d$ polynomials $g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ define projectors
  1422	\[ \hat{S}^X_g = \sum_{g_\zpt} \hat{S}_{g,g_\zpt} \quad  \text{and}  \quad \hat{S}^Z_g = \sum_{g_\xpt} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g}\;,\]
  1423	where the measurement $\{\hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is given by \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}.
  1424	
  1425	For all $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$, and $a \in \F_q$, define the projector
  1426	\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tauwu}
  1427	 \tau^{W}_{a}(\tilde{u}) = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits} \,:\, h \cdot \tilde{u} = a} \tau^W_{h}
  1428	\end{equation}
  1429	where recall that $\tau^W_h$ is the projector corresponding to measuring $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$ in the $W$ basis and obtaining $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ as the outcome. For all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ define the projective measurement $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}_{a \in \F_q}$ by 
  1430		\begin{equation}
  1431		\label{eq:tilde_M}
  1432		\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a =  \sum_{g} \hat{S}^W_g \otimes \tau_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}^W(\tilde{u})\;.
  1433		\end{equation}
  1434		If $\hat{S}^W_g$ is viewed as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice'$ (resp. $\bob \bob'$) then we view $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ (resp. $\bob \bob' \bob''$). (When necessary we will indicate via subscripts which registers the operators are acting on.)
  1435	The $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ are projective because the $\hat{S}^W_g$ and $\tau^W$ operators are projective.

  1438		For all $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$ define the observable

  1463	\begin{lemma}
  1464	  \label{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}

  1467	\begin{enumerate}
  1468	\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, for all $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, and on average over uniformly random $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1469		\[
  1470			\Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \simeq_{\delta_S} M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''}
  1471		\]
  1472		and
  1473		\[
  1474			\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \;.
  1475		\]	
  1476		\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) On average over uniformly random $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$,
  1477		\[
  1478			\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \approx_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})\,.
  1479		\]
  1480	\end{enumerate}
  1481	\end{lemma}

  1483	\begin{proof}

  1485		\begin{align*}
  1486			&\E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_a \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1487			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g,a} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (M^{(\Point,W),u}_a)_{\alice} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u) -a}(\ind_m(u)))_{\bob''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\

  1489			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)})_{\alice \bob''} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1490			&\geq 1 - \delta_S\;.
  1491		\end{align*}

This implies the first item of the Lemma.

  1495	To show the second item we first argue that, on average over $\tilde{u}$, 
  1496		\begin{equation}

  1524		Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-5} follows from~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-4} by expanding the definition of $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a\}$. Next, we argue that, on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,

  1609	We now give a proof of the following Lemma, which was used in several derivations in \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}. 
  1610	\begin{lemma}

  1669	\begin{lemma}
  1670	\label{lem:qld-unitary}
  1671	There exists a function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ (where $\delta_S$ is defined in \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}) and unitaries $V_\alice$ acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ and $V_\bob$ acting on $\bob \bob' \bob''$ such that 
  1672	\begin{enumerate}
  1673		\item There exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1674		\[
  1675			\left \| V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''} - \ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld.
  1676		\]
  1677		
  1678		\item For all $W \in \{X,Z\}, h \in \F_q^\nqubits$
  1679		\begin{align*}
  1680			V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \\
  1681			 V_\bob \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h  \Big)_{\bob}\, V_\bob^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1682		\end{align*}
  1683		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''}$.

  1685	\end{lemma}

  1687	\begin{proof}
  1688	
  1689	Define the linear map
  1690	\[
  1691		V_\alice = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)))_{\alice ''}\;,
  1692	\]
  1693	where the $\tau^X(\cdot),\tau^Z(\cdot)$ act on $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. (Also note that the argument of $\tau^X$ is $\coded(g_Z)$ and the argument of $\tau^Z$ is $\coded(g_X)$.) We verify the unitarity of $V_\alice$:
  1694	\begin{align*}
  1695		V_\alice V_\alice^\dagger &= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) )_{\alice ''} \\
  1696		&= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Id_{\alice ''} \\
  1697		&= \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}
  1698	\end{align*}
  1699	where in the first line we used that the measurement $\{ \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is projective and in the second line we used that the $\tau^Z$ and $\tau^X$ observables are self-inverse. The unitary $V_\bob$ is defined analogously.
  1700	
  1701	Let $\{e_j\}_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}}$ denote the self-dual basis for $\F_q$ over $\F_2$ specified in \Cref{sec:subfields}, and let $\tilde{W}^j$ be the observables introduced in~\eqref{eq:def-tildewj}. Conjugating the observable $\tilde{W}^j$ acting on the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ by the unitary $V_\alice$ we get
  1702	\begin{align*}
  1703		&V_\alice \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\alice^\dagger \\
  1704	  =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1705	  &\hspace{24em}\tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1706		 =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1707		 =& \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''}\;,
  1708	\end{align*}
  1709	where in the third line we used the (anti-)commutation relation
  1710	\[
  1711		\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \;.
  1712	\]

  1714	
  1715	Next, from the self-consistency property of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ specified in \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1716	\[
  1717		\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right)^\dagger \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \leq \delta_S\;,

  1720	\begin{equation}
  1721	\label{eq:qld-unitary-1}
  1722	\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;.
  1723	\end{equation}
  1724	Let $\ket{\vartheta} = V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}$, and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$ define the operator
  1725	\begin{align*}
  1726		H_W &= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \otimes \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1727			&= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} \\

  1729	\end{align*}

  1735	
  1736	Observe that
  1737	\begin{align*}

  1739		&= \E_{s} \sum_{a\in \F_q} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes \ketbra{a+s}{a} \\

  1741	\end{align*}
  1742	where to go from the first to the second line we used \Cref{lem:cancellation}. This implies that $H_X H_Z = \Big ( \E_{s,s' \in \F_q} \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} = \ketbra{\EPR_q}{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1743	By the triangle inequality, we have
  1744	\[
  1745		\left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\| \leq \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_X \ket{\vartheta} \right\| + \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|\;.
  1746	\]
  1747	Note that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1748	\[
  1749		\left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_W \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2 = 1 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} \leq 2 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1750	\]
  1751	where in the inequality we used that $H_W \leq \Id$. Furthermore,
  1752	\begin{align*}
  1753		\bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} &=\| H_W \ket{\vartheta} \|^2\\
  1754		 &= \| \ket{\vartheta} + (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \\
  1755		 &\geq (\|\ket{\vartheta}\| - \| (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|)^2 \\
  1756		 &\geq (1 - \delta_S)^2 \\
  1757		 &\geq 1 - 2\delta_S\;. 
  1758	\end{align*}
  1759	Therefore 
  1760	\begin{align*}
  1761	2\sqrt{\delta_S} &\geq \left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2  \\
  1762	&= \bra{\vartheta} H_X^2 \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_Z^2 \ket{\vartheta} - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1763	&\geq 2 - 4\delta_S - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \;,

  1765	which implies that 
  1766	\[
  1767		\bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S} \;.
  1768	\]
  1769	Define the unnormalized state $\ket{\aux_0}$ on the registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ as
  1770	\[
  1771		\ket{\aux_0}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} = (\bra{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''} \cdot \ket{\vartheta}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''}
  1772	\]
  1773	and define the normalized state $\ket{\aux} = \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \ket{\aux_0}$. 
  1774	The inner product between $\ket{\vartheta}$ and $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$ can thus be evaluated as
  1775	\begin{align*}
  1776		\bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) &= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux_0} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) \\
  1777		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1778		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|^2 \\

  1780		&\geq \sqrt{1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S}} \\

  1784	
  1785	We now establish the second item of the lemma. In what follows, all $\simeq$ and $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$. From \Cref{lem:qld-win-implications} we have the following implications: for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1786		\begin{align}
  1787		\label{eq:qld-unitary-2}
  1788		M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} &\simeq_\eps \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a\;, \\
  1789		\label{eq:qld-unitary-3}

   832	\subsection{Polynomials and the low-degree code}
   833	\label{sec:ld-encoding}
   834	
   835	In this section, we introduce some basic definitions about polynomials over finite fields. 
   836	An $m$-variate polynomial $f$ over $\F_q$ is a function of the form
   837	\[
   838		f(x_1,\ldots,x_m) = \sum_{\alpha \in \{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}^m} c_\alpha
   839	  x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots x_m^{\alpha_m}
   840	\]
   841	where $\{c_\alpha\}$ is a collection of coefficients in $\F_q$.
   842	We say that $f$ has \emph{individual degree (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha\neq 0$ only if
   843	$\alpha_i \leq d $ for all $1\leq i\leq m$, and that it has \emph{total degree
   844	  (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha\neq 0$ only if $\sum_i \alpha_i \leq d$.
   845	(Affine) \emph{multilinear} polynomials are polynomials with individual degree
   846	$1$.
   847	
   848	Low-degree polynomials play an important role in this paper.
   849	For one, the classical and quantum low-degree tests of \Cref{sec:ldt} are
   850	nonlocal games that efficiently certify that the players' answers are consistent
   851	with low-degree polynomials.
   852	Low-degree polynomials are also crucial in the probabilistically checkable
   853	proofs (PCP) construction that are used in ``answer reduction'' transformation
   854	(\Cref{sec:ans}).
   855	
   856	We recall the Schwartz-Zippel lemma: 
   857	
   858	\begin{lemma}[Schwartz-Zippel lemma~\cite{Sch80,Zip79}]
   859	  \label{lem:schwartz-zippel}
   860	  Let $f, g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ be two unequal polynomials with total degree at most $d$. Then
   861	  \begin{equation*}
   862	    \Pr_{x \sim \F_q^m}[f(x) = g(x)] \leq d/q\;.
   863	  \end{equation*}
   864	\end{lemma}
   865	
   866	
   867	\paragraph{The low-degree code.}
   868	The Schwartz-Zippel lemma implies that the set of low-degree polynomials form an
   869	error-correcting code with good distance, which we call the \emph{low-degree
   870	  code}.\footnote{It is also known as the \emph{generalized Reed-Muller code} in
   871	  the coding theory literature.}
   872	
   873	Fix an integer $m \in \N$ and let $M = 2^m$.
   874	For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ define the following $m$-variate multilinear
   875	polynomial over $\F_q$:
   876	\[
   877		\ind_{m,y}(x) = \prod_{i: y_i = 1} x_i \cdot \prod_{i: y_i = 0} (1 - x_i) \;.
   878	\]
   879	Here, we identify $\{0,1\}$ as a subset of $\F_q$.
   880	Notice that, when restricted to the subcube $\{0,1\}^m$, $\ind_{m, y}$ is zero
   881	everywhere except for when $x = y$.
   882	For $a\in \F_q^M$, label the coordinates of $a$ as $a_y$ for $y\in \{0,1\}^m$
   883	(identifying the latter set with $\{1,\ldots,M\}$ using, say, the lexicographic
   884	ordering on strings).
   885	For any such $a$ define the multilinear polynomial $g_a: \F_q^m \to \F_q$,
   886	called the \emph{low-degree encoding of $a$}, as follows:
   887	\begin{equation}
   888	\label{eq:ld-encoding}
   889		 g_a(x) = \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)\;.
   890	\end{equation}
   891	Note that for any $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_a(y) = a_y$.
   892	Furthermore, the map $a\mapsto g_a$ is linear: for every $x \in \F_q^m$,
   893	\begin{equation}
   894	\label{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}
   895		g_a(x) = a \cdot \ind_m(x)\;,
   896	\end{equation}
   897	where $\ind_m(x)$ is the vector $(\ind_{m,y}(x))_{y \in \{0,1\}^m}\in\F_q^M$.
   898	
   899	\begin{lemma}
   900	\label{lem:ld-encoding-complexity}
   901	Let $q$ be an admissible field size, and let $M = 2^m$ for some integer $m$.
   902	The complexity of computing the evaluation of the low-degree encoding $g_a(x)$,
   903	given $a \in \F_q^M$ and $x \in \F_q^m$ represented in binary, is $\poly(M,\log
   904	q)$.
   905	\end{lemma}
   906	\begin{proof}
   907		Computing $g_a(x)$ requires computing the sum of products $a_y \cdot
   908	  \ind_{m,y}(x)$ over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$.
   909	  Via \Cref{lem:efficient_arithmetic}, evaluating $\ind_{m,y}(x)$ takes time
   910	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ because it requires performing $m$ multiplications of $\F_q$
   911	  elements, and therefore the product $a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)$ requires
   912	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ time.
   913	  Computing the sum over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ requires $M \cdot \poly(m,\log q)
   914	  = \poly(M,\log q)$ time, as claimed.
   915	\end{proof}
   916

   919	returns the following vector $a \in \F_q^M$: for all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, if $g(y)
   920	\in H$, then set $a_y = g(y)$, and otherwise set $a_y = 0$.
   921	Note that for all $a \in H^M$ we have $\coded_H(g_a) = a$ where $g_a$ is the
   922	low-degree encoding of $a$.
   923	For notational brevity we often write $\coded(\cdot)$ to denote the boolean
   924	decoding map $\coded_{\{0,1\}}(\cdot)$.

   228

   231	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:216-230`, paper
   232	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1687-1713`. -/
   233	noncomputable def conjBy {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
   234	    (V N : Op ι) : Op ι :=
   235	  V * N * Vᴴ

   238	a global polynomial-pair witness. Here `deltaG` is its consistency error. The
   239	remaining terms record the point-measurement transfer
   240	and the Schwartz--Zippel loss; when `0 ≤ epsilon ≤ 1`, `sqrt epsilon` also
   241	dominates terms of order `epsilon`.
   242	
   243	This makes explicit the enlargement of the error called `deltaS` in
   244	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`, blueprint
   245	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:120-196`, paper

   247	noncomputable def deltaConstructPaulis (C epsilon deltaG : ℝ)

   250	    ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))

   252	/-- The explicit extraction scale
   253	`C * (deltaS^(1/4) + md/q)` from `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
   254	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
   255	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   256	noncomputable def deltaExtract (C deltaS : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   257	  C * (Real.rpow deltaS (1 / 4 : ℝ) + ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (q : ℝ))

    11	families remain complete measurements. The winning hypothesis bounds their
    12	original wrong-form mass by the rejection probability. `Option` is used only
    13	for the completed line-evaluation classes.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The ambient strategy convention and the observable `W^r(u)` are in
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-190`,
    19	corresponding to `def:strategy-observables` in
    20	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:480-503`. The typed question
    21	and answer forms come from `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
    22	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, paper
    23	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`
    24	and blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-392`.
    25	-/

    28	
    29	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    33	noncomputable section
    34	
    35	/-- The two local registers of a heterogeneous bipartite strategy. This is
    36	formalization-only indexing for the player-dependent notation at paper
    37	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-190`. -/
    38	inductive PlayerSide where
    39	  | alice
    40	  | bob
    41	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    42	
    43	/-- A projective strategy satisfying the winning premise used throughout
    44	Section `sec:commutation`. The structure retains the distinct player spaces and
    45	measurement families of `Strategy`. Paper
    46	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-172`; blueprint
    47	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:385-475`. -/
    48	structure ProjectiveSetting (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) where
    49	  toStrategy : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)
    50	  isProjective : toStrategy.IsProjective
    51	  win : 1 - ε ≤ toStrategy.value

    53	namespace ProjectiveSetting

    55	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}

    57	/-- The local Hilbert-space index type on a specified player side. It indexes
    58	the side-qualified operators at paper
    59	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190`. -/
    60	def LocalSpace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) : PlayerSide → Type
    61	  | .alice => S.toStrategy.ιA
    62	  | .bob => S.toStrategy.ιB
    63	
    64	instance localSpaceFintype (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :
    65	    Fintype (S.LocalSpace side) := by
    66	  cases side <;> simp only [LocalSpace] <;> infer_instance
    67	
    68	instance localSpaceDecidableEq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :
    69	    DecidableEq (S.LocalSpace side) := by
    70	  cases side <;> simp only [LocalSpace] <;> infer_instance
    71	
    72	/-- Select the strategy measurement before outcome postprocessing on one
    73	player side. This is the heterogeneous interpretation of the shared symbol `M` at
    74	paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:160-184`. -/
    75	def strategyMeasurement (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    76	    (question : PauliQuestion P) :
    77	    Measurement (PauliAnswer P) (S.LocalSpace side) := by
    78	  cases side with
    79	  | alice => exact S.toStrategy.A question
    80	  | bob => exact S.toStrategy.B question
    81	
    82	/-- Embed a point into the full Pauli question space in basis `W`. This is the
    83	point-question content from `def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper
    84	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`, blueprint
    85	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`. -/
    86	def contentOfPoint (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    87	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : PauliSpace P :=
    88	  embedLd P W fun i =>
    89	    match i with
    90	    | .inl (.inl j) => u j
    91	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
    92	    | .inr _ => 0
    93	
    94	/-- Embed a canonical line description into the full Pauli question space.
    95	Axis lines clear the direction block, whereas diagonal lines retain their
    96	canonical projected direction. Paper
    97	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:997-1008`; blueprint
    98	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354` and `rem:deg-line-representatives`. -/
    99	def contentOfLine (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   100	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) : PauliSpace P :=
   101	  embedLd P W fun i =>
   102	    match i with
   103	    | .inl (.inl j) => line.base j
   104	    | .inl (.inr _) => line.seed
   105	    | .inr j =>
   106	        match line with
   107	        | .axis _ _ _ => 0
   108	        | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction j
   109	
   110	/-- Fill the point, scalar, and phase blocks shared by Pair, Pair/W, and Magic
   111	Square questions. This is the type-4 content of
   112	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, paper
   113	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1030-1120`, blueprint
   114	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`. -/
   115	def contentOfTuple (P : AdmissibleParams)
   116	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : PauliSpace P :=
   117	  fun i =>
   118	    match i with
   119	    | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) => uX j
   120	    | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) => uZ j
   121	    | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => 0
   122	    | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
   123	    | .inl (.inr _) => rX
   124	    | .inr _ => rZ
   125	
   126	/-- The typed point question in basis `W`, from the strategy notation at paper
   127	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-190` and
   128	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:310-354`. -/
   129	def pointQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   130	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : PauliQuestion P :=
   131	  (.point W, contentOfPoint P W u)
   132	
   133	/-- The typed axis or diagonal line question represented by a canonical
   134	`LineDesc`. Paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:174-184`; blueprint
   135	`def:strategy-observables` and `rem:deg-line-representatives`. -/
   136	def lineQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   137	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) : PauliQuestion P :=
   138	  match line.kind with
   139	  | .axis => (.aline W, contentOfLine P W line)
   140	  | .diagonal => (.dline W, contentOfLine P W line)
   141	
   142	/-- The typed Pair question for a tuple `(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)`. Paper
   143	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-249`; blueprint
   144	`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
   145	def pairQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams)
   146	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : PauliQuestion P :=
   147	  (.pair, contentOfTuple P uX uZ rX rZ)

   149	/-- The typed Pair/W question for a tuple `(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)`. Paper
   150	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:210-249`; blueprint
   151	`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/

   153	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : PauliQuestion P :=
   154	  (.pairW W, contentOfTuple P uX uZ rX rZ)

   156	/-- The typed Magic Square question for a tuple `(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)`. Paper
   157	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:213-258`; blueprint
   158	`lem:qld-win-implications`. -/
   159	def msQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : MsType)
   160	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : PauliQuestion P :=
   161	  (.ms t, contentOfTuple P uX uZ rX rZ)

   169	  ∃ other : PauliQuestion P,

   177	theorem pointQuestion_appears_in_support (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   178	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   179	    QuestionAppearsInSupport P (pointQuestion P W u) := by

     6	
     7	This module contains the quantitative error function and the closed definitions

    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The interface supports `thm:pauli` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, with paper origin
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.

    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    30	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    31	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    32	as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`,
    33	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    34	-/
    35	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    36	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    37	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    38	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    39

    41	`deltaQld` on the source parameter domain. This Lean-only helper supports the

    43	Chapter 16 preamble (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:101-104`);
    44	the source makes this constant adjustment at
    45	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1402`. It is not
    46	an additional hypothesis of `thm:pauli` or `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    47	theorem deltaQld_mono {P : AdmissibleParams} {a a' b b' ε : ℝ}
    48	    (ha0 : 1 ≤ a) (ha : a ≤ a') (hb : b' ≤ b) (hb' : 0 < b')
    49	    (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :
    50	    deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ≤ deltaQld a' b' ε P.m P.d P.q := by
    51	  sorry
    52	
    53	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    54	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
    55	`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:537-547`; paper
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    57	-/
    58	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    59	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    60	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    61	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    62	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    63	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
    64	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    65	    (fun p =>
    66	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    67	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
    68	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
    69	
    70	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
    71	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
    72	in `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`; paper

    74	-/
    75	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    76	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    77	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    78	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    79	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    80	  fun p q =>
    81	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
    82	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
    83	    else 0

    86	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, paper origin
    87	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.

    89	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    90	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    91	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    92	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    93	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    94	  fun p q =>
    95	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
    96	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
    97	    else 0
    98	
    99	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   100	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, paper origin
   101	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   102	-/
   103	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   104	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   105	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   106	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   107	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   108	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   109	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   110	  fun p q =>
   111	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   112	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   113	    else 0

   117	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.

   119	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}

     4	/-!
     5	# Expanded registers and point measurements
     6	
     7	This module adjoins two EPR pairs to a heterogeneous Pauli-basis-test strategy,
     8	records the four register placements used in the analysis, and defines the
     9	expanded point observables and measurements.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The constructions formalize `def:expanded-state`, `def:expanded-observables`,
    14	`def:expanded-point-measurement`, and `def:expanded-point-trace-projection` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-874`. Their paper source is
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-418`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- The six registers `AA'A''BB'B''`, retaining distinct Alice and Bob local
    28	spaces. This is the register index type of `def:expanded-state`, paper
    29	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    30	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    31	abbrev SixReg (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
    32	  (ιA × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    33	    (ιB × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P))
    34	
    35	/-- Equality of six-register indices is supplied by classical decidability for
    36	the register type. This is the index set of `def:expanded-state`; blueprint
    37	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    38	noncomputable instance sixRegDecidableEq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    39	    (ιA ιB : Type*) : DecidableEq (SixReg P ιA ιB) :=
    40	  Classical.decEq _
    41	
    42	/-- Reassociate the tensor product of the strategy state and two EPR states
    43	directly into register order `AA'A''BB'B''` for
    44	`eq:def-psihat`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`. -/
    45	def sixRegShuffle (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    46	    (((ιA × ιB) × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    47	        (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
    48	  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    49	    (p.1.1.2, (p.2.1, p.2.2)))
    50	  invFun p := (((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    51	    (p.2.2.1, p.2.2.2))
    52	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    53	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    54	
    55	/-- The four placements `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, and `AB''` used explicitly in
    56	the chapter-14 consistency statements. Paper
    57	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
    58	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
    59	inductive Placement where
    60	  | AA'
    61	  | BA''
    62	  | BB'
    63	  | AB''
    64	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    65	
    66	/-- The strategy-player side supplying the local Hilbert space in each of the
    67	four register placements at paper
    68	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`. -/
    69	def Placement.side : Placement → PlayerSide
    70	  | .AA' => .alice
    71	  | .BA'' => .bob
    72	  | .BB' => .bob
    73	  | .AB'' => .alice
    74	
    75	namespace ProjectiveSetting
    76	
    77	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    78	
    79	/-- A strategy-local register paired with one generalized-Pauli register. This
    80	is the operator space in `def:expanded-observables`, paper
    81	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`. -/
    82	abbrev ExpandedLocalSpace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :=
    83	  S.LocalSpace side × PauliRegister P
    84	
    85	/-- The strategy state tensored with EPR states on `A'A''` and `B'B''`, in the
    86	six-register order. This is `eq:def-psihat`, paper
    87	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    88	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    89	noncomputable def psiHat (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    90	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
    91	  classical
    92	  exact
    93	    reindexState (sixRegShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    94	      (vecTensor
    95	        (vecTensor S.toStrategy.ψ (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    96	        (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    97	
    98	/-- Place an operator on one of `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, or `AB''`, with the
    99	identity on all remaining registers. The input local space is determined by
   100	the placement, so no equality between the player spaces is assumed. Paper
   101	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
   102	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
   103	noncomputable def place (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
   104	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
   105	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   106	  fun i j =>
   107	    match p with
   108	    | .AA' =>
   109	        O (i.1.1, i.1.2.1) (j.1.1, j.1.2.1) *
   110	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   111	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   112	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   113	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   114	    | .BA'' =>
   115	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   116	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   117	          O (i.2.1, i.1.2.2) (j.2.1, j.1.2.2) *
   118	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   119	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   120	    | .BB' =>
   121	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   122	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   123	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   124	          O (i.2.1, i.2.2.1) (j.2.1, j.2.2.1) *
   125	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   126	    | .AB'' =>
   127	        O (i.1.1, i.2.2.2) (j.1.1, j.2.2.2) *
   128	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   129	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   130	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   131	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1
   132	
   133	/-- The expanded observable
   134	`W^r(u) tensor tau^W(r * ind_m(u))` on a selected player side. This is
   135	Equation `eq:lc-23`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`,
   136	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:783-807`. -/
   137	noncomputable def expObs (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   138	    (W : PauliKind) (r : PauliScalar P) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   139	    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   140	  heteroKron (S.pointObs side W r u)
   141	    (tauObservable W (fun h => r * indicatorVec u h))
   142	
   143	/-- The Fourier average defining the expanded point effect. This is the first
   144	display of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   145	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`, blueprint
   146	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   147	noncomputable def expPointOp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   148	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   149	    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   150	  averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P)) fun r =>
   151	    phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)) • S.expObs side W r u
   152	
   153	/-- The Pauli-register projector onto labels whose low-degree encoding has
   154	value `a` at `u`. This is Equation `eq:qld-point-obs-def`, paper
   155	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:389-394`, blueprint
   156	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   157	noncomputable def tauPointProj (W : PauliKind)
   158	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (PauliRegister P) :=
   159	  ∑ h ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun h : PauliRegister P =>
   160	      dotProduct h (indicatorVec u) = a),
   161	    pauliProj W h
   162	
   163	/-- Expanded point effects are positive semidefinite. This is the positivity
   164	obligation in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   165	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   166	theorem expPointOp_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   167	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   168	    0 ≤ S.expPointOp side W u a := by
   169	  sorry
   170	
   171	/-- Expanded point effects sum to the identity. This is the completeness
   172	obligation in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   173	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   174	theorem expPointOp_sum_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   175	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   176	    ∑ a, S.expPointOp side W u a = 1 := by
   177	  sorry
   178	
   179	/-- The complete expanded point measurement on the chosen player and Pauli
   180	register. Its effects are those of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   181	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`, blueprint
   182	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   183	noncomputable def pointMeasExp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   184	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   185	    Measurement (PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   186	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (S.expPointOp side W u)
   187	    (S.expPointOp_nonneg side W u) (S.expPointOp_sum_eq_one side W u)
   188	
   189	/-- The expanded point effect is the convolution of the strategy point
   190	measurement and the Pauli-register point projection. This is the final display
   191	of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   192	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:395-418`. -/
   193	theorem expPointOp_eq_convolution (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   194	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   195	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
   196	    S.expPointOp side W u a =
   197	      ∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P =>
   198	          p.1 + p.2 = a),
   199	        heteroKron ((S.pointMeas side W u).effect p.1)
   200	          (tauPointProj W u p.2) := by
   201	  sorry
   202	
   203	/-- The expanded point measurement is projective, as asserted after the
   204	convolution formula in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   205	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:395-418`. -/
   206	theorem pointMeasExp_isProjective (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   207	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   208	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.pointMeasExp side W u) := by
   209	  sorry
   210	
   211	/-- Trace-coarse-graining of the expanded point measurement. This is Equation
   212	`eq:qld-def-mptur`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:411-418`,
   213	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:846-874`. -/
   214	noncomputable def expPointTrace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   215	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   216	    (r : PauliScalar P) : Measurement (ZMod 2) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   217	  (S.pointMeasExp side W u).postprocess fun a => fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)
   218	
   219	/-- Fourier inversion writes a trace-coarse-grained point effect as one half
   220	of the identity plus its signed expanded observable. This is Equation
   221	`eq:lc-22`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:411-418`, blueprint
   222	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:846-874`. -/
   223	theorem expPointTrace_eq_half_add (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   224	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   225	    (r : PauliScalar P) (b : ZMod 2) :
   226	    (S.expPointTrace side W u r).effect b =
   227	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   228	        (1 + phaseSign b • S.expObs side W r u) := by
   229	  sorry

     4	/-!
     5	# Generalized Pauli operators and EPR states
     6	
     7	The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
     8	are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
     9	operator algebra.  The Fourier/orthogonality identities are retained as named
    10	proof obligations for subsequent stages.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The source-facing nodes are `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`, `def:generalized-pauli`,
    15	and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:494-652`.  The paper origin is
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    27	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    28	
    29	/-- The two generalized Pauli bases used by the test in `def:generalized-pauli`,
    30	blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    31	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    32	-/
    33	inductive PauliKind where
    34	  | X
    35	  | Z
    36	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    37	
    38	/-- The binary character used for generalized Pauli phases; see
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1081`.
    40	
    41	It is public because the Fourier expansion declarations below expose this
    42	character in their statement types. -/
    43	noncomputable def phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    44	  if t = 0 then 1 else -1
    45	
    46	/--
    47	The shift operator `τ^X(a)`.  Blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`,
    48	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`; paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    50	-/
    51	noncomputable def tauShift (a : K) : Op K :=
    52	  fun i j => if i = j + a then 1 else 0
    53	
    54	/--
    55	The phase operator `τ^Z(b)`, with the fixed binary trace in the phase.  It is
    56	the second operator of `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 529-571; paper
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`).
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def tauPhase (b : K) : Op K :=
    60	  fun i j => if i = j then phaseSign (binTrace K (b * j)) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- The single-qudit eigenvector coordinate used in the tensor-product basis;
    63	see `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1126-1161`. -/
    64	private noncomputable def singlePauliVec (W : PauliKind) (e x : K) : ℂ :=
    65	  match W with
    66	  | .Z => if x = e then 1 else 0
    67	  | .X =>
    68	      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * phaseSign (binTrace K (e * x))
    69	
    70	/--
    71	The normalized single/multi-qudit eigenvector for a Pauli basis label.  For an
    72	index type `ι`, the input `e : ι → K` labels the tensor-product basis vector.
    73	This is the vector form of `def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint
    74	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:550-570`, paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`.
    76	-/
    77	noncomputable def pauliVec {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    78	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) (x : ι → K) : ℂ :=
    79	  ∏ i : ι, singlePauliVec W (e i) (x i)
    80	
    81	/--
    82	The rank-one projector onto `pauliVec W e`.  This is the projective measurement
    83	element `τ^W_e` in `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 562-570; paper
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`).
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    87	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    88	  Matrix.vecMulVec (pauliVec W e) (fun x => star (pauliVec W e x))
    89	
    90	/-- A compact operator-valued form of a generalized Pauli observable from
    91	`def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    93	-/
    94	noncomputable def tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    95	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    96	  fun x y =>
    97	    ∏ i : ι,
    98	      match W with
    99	      | .X => tauShift (a i) (x i) (y i)
   100	      | .Z => tauPhase (a i) (x i) (y i)
   101	
   102	/--
   103	The EPR vector on a finite label space.  Blueprint `def:EPR`,
   104	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper origin
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
   106	-/
   107	noncomputable def eprState (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   108	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (V × V) :=
   109	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (V × V) ℂ).symm
   110	    (fun p : V × V =>
   111	      if p.1 = p.2 then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0)
   112	
   113	/-- The EPR vector is normalized on a nonempty finite carrier; see
   114	`def:EPR`, `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`. -/
   115	theorem eprState_norm (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   116	    ‖eprState V‖ = 1 := by
   117	  sorry
   118	
   119	/--
   120	Fourier expansion of a generalized Pauli observable in the Pauli projectors.
   121	This is `lem:pauli-observable-expansion`, equations `eq:pauli-obs-proj` and
   122	`eq:pauli-inversion-0`, in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:638-652`;
   123	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1141-1161`.
   124	Both directions are deliberately left as proof-level obligations in stage 4.1.
   125	-/
   126	theorem tauObservable_eq_sum_pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   127	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) :
   128	    tauObservable W a =
   129	      ∑ e : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • pauliProj W e := by
   130	  sorry
   131	
   132	/-- The inverse Fourier expansion of a Pauli projector
   133	(`lem:pauli-observable-expansion`), blueprint
   134	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:638-652`, paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1141-1161`.
   136	-/
   137	theorem pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   138	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) :
   139	    pauliProj W e =
   140	      (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   141	        ∑ a : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • tauObservable W a := by
   142	  sorry
   143	
   144	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

280	  /-- The complete extended-line measurement on each player side. -/
   281	  Qline : (side : PlayerSide) -> DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ->
   282	    Measurement (DirectDegPoly P.extendedDirectLd (P.m * P.d + 1))
   283	      (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
   284	  /-- Axis-line outcomes outside degree `d` have zero effect. -/
   285	  axis_degree : ∀ side line f, line.kind = .axis ->
   286	    Not (∀ i, P.d < i.val -> f i = 0) ->
   287	      (Qline side line).effect f = 0
   288	  /-- Alice's evaluated line measurement is consistent with Bob's completed
   289	  combined point measurement. -/
   290	  consistent_alice : consistencyDefect
   291	    (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd)
   292	    (fun sample answer => S.place .AA'
   293	      (((Qline .alice sample.1).postprocess
   294	        (fun f => (directEvalOpt sample.1 sample.2 f).map
   295	          (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P))).effect answer))
   296	    (fun sample answer => S.place .BA''
   297	      (((points.Q .bob
   298	        (projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   299	        (projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))).postprocess fun ab =>
   300	          some (directPointToPauli P sample.2 (alphaVar P.m) * ab.1 +
   301	            directPointToPauli P sample.2 (betaVar P.m) * ab.2)).effect answer))
   302	    S.psiHat <= δ
   303	  /-- Bob's evaluated line measurement is consistent with Alice's completed
   304	  combined point measurement. -/
   305	  consistent_bob : consistencyDefect
   306	    (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd)
   307	    (fun sample answer => S.place .BB'
   308	      (((Qline .bob sample.1).postprocess
   309	        (fun f => (directEvalOpt sample.1 sample.2 f).map
   310	          (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P))).effect answer))
   311	    (fun sample answer => S.place .AB''
   312	      (((points.Q .alice
   313	        (projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   314	        (projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))).postprocess fun ab =>
   315	          some (directPointToPauli P sample.2 (alphaVar P.m) * ab.1 +
   316	            directPointToPauli P sample.2 (betaVar P.m) * ab.2)).effect answer))
   317	    S.psiHat <= δ
   318	
   319	/-- The side-indexed global polynomial-pair measurements handed to Chapter 16.
   320	This is the exact conclusion of `lem:qld-4-7`, paper lines 1267--1274, with
   321	the two heterogeneous point-consistency displays stated separately. -/
   322	structure GlobalPairWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
   323	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (δ : ℝ) where
   324	  /-- The complete global polynomial-pair measurement on each player side. -/
   325	  Smeas : (side : PlayerSide) ->
   326	    Measurement (PolyPair P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
   327	  /-- Both global polynomial-pair measurements are projective. -/
   328	  projective : ∀ side, Measurement.IsProjective (Smeas side)
   329	  /-- Alice's global evaluations are consistent with Bob's source point
   330	  measurements, for each Pauli basis. -/
   331	  point_consistent_alice : ∀ W : PauliKind,
   332	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P))
   333	      (fun u a => S.place .AA'
   334	        (((Smeas .alice).postprocess (evalAt W u)).effect a))
   335	      (fun u a => S.place .BA''
   336	        ((S.pointMeasExp .bob W u).effect a))
   337	      S.psiHat <= δ
   338	  /-- Bob's global evaluations are consistent with Alice's source point
   339	  measurements, for each Pauli basis. -/
   340	  point_consistent_bob : ∀ W : PauliKind,
   341	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P))
   342	      (fun u a => S.place .BB'
   343	        (((Smeas .bob).postprocess (evalAt W u)).effect a))
   344	      (fun u a => S.place .AB''
   345	        ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect a))
   346	      S.psiHat <= δ
   347	
   348	end
   349	
   350	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Quantitative state and operator distances
     5	
     6	The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
     7	corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
     8	estimates to later proof stages.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    23	
    24	/--
    25	Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
    26	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    28	-/
    29	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    30	    [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    32	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    33	
    34	/--
    35	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    36	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
    37	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    38	-/
    39	noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    40	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    41	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    42	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    43	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    44	    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)
    45	
    46	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.LowDegreeCode
     2	
     3	/-! # Decoding maps for the low-degree code
     4	
     5	This file supplies `def:decoding-map` and the Boolean cube embedding from
     6	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
     7	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`.  The specialization to
     8	polynomial representatives is `decodeFqRep`; its restriction to the bounded
     9	class `Poly` is defined in `Algebra/Decoding`.
    10	-/
    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    15	
    16	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    17	
    18	/-- The formalization-only embedding of Boolean coordinates into a field used by
    19	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    20	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    21	def boolToScalar {K : Type*} [Field K] : Bool → K
    22	  | false => 0
    23	  | true => 1
    24	
    25	/-- The coordinatewise Boolean-cube embedding used by
    26	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    27	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    28	def cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} : Cube m → (Fin m → K) :=
    29	  fun y i => boolToScalar (y i)
    30	
    31	/-- On the Boolean cube, an indicator polynomial evaluates to the corresponding
    32	Kronecker delta.  This is the interpolation observation at paper lines 880-891. -/
    33	private theorem eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    34	    (y z : Cube m) :
    35	    MvPolynomial.eval (cubeEmbed (K := K) z) (indicatorPoly (K := K) y) =
    36	      if y = z then 1 else 0 := by
    37	  classical
    38	  rw [indicatorPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_prod]
    39	  simp only [apply_ite, MvPolynomial.eval_X, MvPolynomial.eval_sub, map_one]
    40	  have hfactor (i : Fin m) :
    41	      (if y i then cubeEmbed (K := K) z i else 1 - cubeEmbed (K := K) z i) =
    42	        if y i = z i then 1 else 0 := by
    43	    cases hy : y i <;> cases hz : z i <;> simp_all [cubeEmbed, boolToScalar]
    44	  simp_rw [hfactor]
    45	  rw [Fintype.prod_boole]
    46	  split_ifs <;> simp_all [funext_iff]
    47	
    48	/-- Evaluating a low-degree encoding at an embedded Boolean point recovers its
    49	coefficient at that point, as stated at paper line 891. -/
    50	private theorem lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    51	    (a : Cube m → K) (z : Cube m) :
    52	    lowDegreeEnc a (cubeEmbed z) = a z := by
    53	  rw [lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct]
    54	  simp [dotProduct, indicatorVec, eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed]
    55	
    56	/-- The decoding map `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    57	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    58	noncomputable def decodeAt {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    59	    (H : Finset K) (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    60	  fun y => if g (cubeEmbed y) ∈ H then g (cubeEmbed y) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- Boolean specialization of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    63	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    64	noncomputable abbrev decodeBool {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    65	    (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    66	  decodeAt ({0, 1} : Finset K) g
    67	
    68	/-- The full-field specialization of `decodeAt` used by the generic algebra
    69	layer.  The Chapter 16 `Poly`-facing name is defined in `Algebra/Decoding.lean`.
    70	Every value is retained because the filter is `H = Finset.univ`, so this is the
    71	cube-indexed evaluation of a polynomial representative.  The restricted
    72	decoder identity remains separate and is only available for encoding
    73	representatives; no unrestricted interpolation identity is asserted here.
    74	
    75	This is the `H = \F_q` reading of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    76	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, used by Chapter 16 at
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:11-20`; paper origin
    78	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1420` and
    79	the correction recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`. -/
    80	noncomputable def decodeFqRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    81	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Cube m → K :=
    82	  decodeAt (Finset.univ : Finset K) (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x g)
    83	
    84	/-- A polynomial representative lies in the low-degree encoding image when it
    85	is exactly the multilinear representative reconstructed from its full-field
    86	decoder.  This predicate is used to state the support restriction required by
    87	the Chapter 16 decoding argument; it does not identify arbitrary polynomial
    88	functions with their representatives.
    89	
    90	See `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-116`. -/
    91	def IsEncodingRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    92	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Prop :=
    93	  lowDegreeEncoding (decodeFqRep g) = g
    94	
    95	/-- The restricted decoding identity in `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    96	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    97	theorem decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    98	    (H : Finset K) (a : Cube m → K) (ha : ∀ y, a y ∈ H) :
    99	    decodeAt H (lowDegreeEnc a) = a := by
   100	  funext y
   101	  simp [decodeAt, lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed, ha y]
   102	
   103	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# The low-degree encoding
     5	
     6	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials
     7	and packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The source-facing nodes are `def:polynomials-degree`,
    12	`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:321-417`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    15	The polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from
    16	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	open MvPolynomial
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
    25	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    26	type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
    27	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    29	-/
    30	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
    34	zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in
    35	`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    39	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    40	  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)
    41	
    42	/--
    43	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    44	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    45	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    50	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    51	  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y
    52	
    53	/- Evaluation shorthand for the representative polynomial in
    54	`def:low-degree-encoding`; it is Lean-only notation. -/
    55	/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    60	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=
    61	  eval x (lowDegreeEncoding a)
    62	
    63	/--
    64	The indicator vector `ind_m(x)` of `def:indicator-vector`.
    65	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`; paper origin:
    66	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    67	-/
    68	noncomputable def indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    69	    (x : Fin m → K) : Cube m → K :=
    70	  fun y => eval x (indicatorPoly y)
    71	
    72	/--
    73	The defining dot-product identity for the encoding, corresponding to
    74	Equation `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` and `def:indicator-vector` in the
    75	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`, paper origin
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    77	-/
    78	theorem lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    79	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) :
    80	    lowDegreeEnc a x = dotProduct a (indicatorVec x) := by
    81	  simp [lowDegreeEnc, lowDegreeEncoding, indicatorVec, dotProduct]
    82	
    83	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Observables.Defs
     3	
     4	/-!
     5	# Expanded registers and point measurements
     6	
     7	This module adjoins two EPR pairs to a heterogeneous Pauli-basis-test strategy,
     8	records the four register placements used in the analysis, and defines the
     9	expanded point observables and measurements.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The constructions formalize `def:expanded-state`, `def:expanded-observables`,
    14	`def:expanded-point-measurement`, and `def:expanded-point-trace-projection` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-874`. Their paper source is
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-418`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- The six registers `AA'A''BB'B''`, retaining distinct Alice and Bob local
    28	spaces. This is the register index type of `def:expanded-state`, paper
    29	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    30	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    31	abbrev SixReg (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
    32	  (ιA × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    33	    (ιB × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P))
    34	
    35	/-- Equality of six-register indices is supplied by classical decidability for
    36	the register type. This is the index set of `def:expanded-state`; blueprint
    37	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    38	noncomputable instance sixRegDecidableEq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    39	    (ιA ιB : Type*) : DecidableEq (SixReg P ιA ιB) :=
    40	  Classical.decEq _
    41	
    42	/-- Reassociate the tensor product of the strategy state and two EPR states
    43	directly into register order `AA'A''BB'B''` for
    44	`eq:def-psihat`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`. -/
    45	def sixRegShuffle (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    46	    (((ιA × ιB) × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    47	        (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
    48	  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    49	    (p.1.1.2, (p.2.1, p.2.2)))
    50	  invFun p := (((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    51	    (p.2.2.1, p.2.2.2))
    52	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    53	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    54	
    55	/-- The four placements `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, and `AB''` used explicitly in
    56	the chapter-14 consistency statements. Paper
    57	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
    58	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
    59	inductive Placement where
    60	  | AA'
    61	  | BA''
    62	  | BB'
    63	  | AB''
    64	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    65	
    66	/-- The strategy-player side supplying the local Hilbert space in each of the
    67	four register placements at paper
    68	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`. -/
    69	def Placement.side : Placement → PlayerSide
    70	  | .AA' => .alice
    71	  | .BA'' => .bob
    72	  | .BB' => .bob
    73	  | .AB'' => .alice
    74	
    75	namespace ProjectiveSetting
    76	
    77	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    78	
    79	/-- A strategy-local register paired with one generalized-Pauli register. This
    80	is the operator space in `def:expanded-observables`, paper
    81	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`. -/
    82	abbrev ExpandedLocalSpace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :=
    83	  S.LocalSpace side × PauliRegister P
    84	
    85	/-- The strategy state tensored with EPR states on `A'A''` and `B'B''`, in the
    86	six-register order. This is `eq:def-psihat`, paper
    87	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    88	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    89	noncomputable def psiHat (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    90	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
    91	  classical
    92	  exact
    93	    reindexState (sixRegShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    94	      (vecTensor
    95	        (vecTensor S.toStrategy.ψ (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    96	        (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    97	
    98	/-- Place an operator on one of `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, or `AB''`, with the
    99	identity on all remaining registers. The input local space is determined by
   100	the placement, so no equality between the player spaces is assumed. Paper
   101	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
   102	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
   103	noncomputable def place (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
   104	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
   105	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   106	  fun i j =>
   107	    match p with
   108	    | .AA' =>
   109	        O (i.1.1, i.1.2.1) (j.1.1, j.1.2.1) *
   110	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   111	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   112	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   113	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   114	    | .BA'' =>
   115	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   116	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   117	          O (i.2.1, i.1.2.2) (j.2.1, j.1.2.2) *
   118	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   119	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   120	    | .BB' =>
   121	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   122	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   123	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   124	          O (i.2.1, i.2.2.1) (j.2.1, j.2.2.1) *
   125	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2

    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low.  The source drops a nontrivial phase when the
    23	  two binary-basis indices are distinct.
    24	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One exact multiplication calculation for
    25	  generalized Pauli observables; no robustness estimate changes.
    26	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite-sum bilinearity and the field
    27	  trace are standard algebra.  The extracted-observable product form and the
    28	  project's phase convention are project-local.
    29	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The generalized Pauli commutation
    30	  relation and nondegeneracy of the trace pairing.  The local correction is
    31	  tracked in \ghissue{19}.
    32	\end{itemize}
    33	
    34	\section{Key theorem forms}
    35	
    36	Let $e_0,\ldots,e_{t-1}$ be the fixed self-dual basis of $\mathbb F_q$ over
    37	$\mathbb F_2$.  With the phase convention of the source, generalized Pauli
    38	observables satisfy
    39	\[
    40	  \tau^X(a)\tau^Z(b)
    41	  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(a\mathbin{\cdot}b)}
    42	   \tau^Z(b)\tau^X(a).
    43	\]
    44	Substituting $a=e_j\widetilde u$ and $b=e_{j'}\widetilde v$ gives the exact
    45	relation
    46	\[
    47	  \widetilde X^j(\widetilde u)\widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)
    48	  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}
    49	      (e_je_{j'}(\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v))}
    50	   \widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)\widetilde X^j(\widetilde u).
    51	\]
    52	This formula applies uniformly, whether or not $j=j'$.
    53	
    54	\section{The false dichotomy in the source}
    55	
    56	Lines~1438--1450 of
    57	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    58	identify each extracted observable with a tensor product containing
    59	$\tau^W(e_j\widetilde u)$.  Lines~1451--1456 then claim that the extracted
    60	$X$- and $Z$-observables commute whenever $j\neq j'$
    61	\cite[lines~1438--1456]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  Self-duality gives only
    62	\[
    63	  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'})=0 \qquad (j\neq j').
    64	\]
    65	It does not imply
    66	\[
    67	  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'}s)=0
    68	  \qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb F_q.
    69	\]
    70	
    71	Indeed, for distinct $j,j'$, the element $c=e_je_{j'}$ is nonzero.  The trace
    72	pairing is nondegenerate, so there is an $s\in\mathbb F_q$ for which
    73	$\operatorname{tr}(cs)=1$.  Taking vectors whose first coordinates are $1$
    74	and $s$, with all remaining coordinates zero, gives
    75	$\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v=s$.  The two extracted observables
    76	then anticommute.  This is a counterexample to the printed cross-basis
    77	commutation assertion.
    78	
    79	When $\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v$ lies in the prime field, the
    80	printed distinction is recovered from self-duality.  The chapter quantifies
    81	over arbitrary vectors, however, so that special case does not repair its
    82	statement.
    83	
    84	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
    85	
    86	Equation~\path{eq:tildew-twisted-commutation} and
    87	Remark~\path{rem:qld-cross-phase} in
    88	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} record the full phase and
    89	note that the false dichotomy is not used later in the extraction argument.
    90	The declaration \path{tildeObs_twisted_commutation} in
    91	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Observables.lean} quantifies
    92	$j,j'$ over the zero-based type
    93	$\operatorname{Fin}(\texttt{P.model.basisDim})$ and concludes exactly the
    94	uniform phase relation displayed above.  Its docstring carries the required
    95	\textbf{Local fix} marker.  Thus the Lean statement agrees with the corrected
    96	blueprint and deliberately differs from the false cross-basis commutation
    97	claim in the paper; it introduces no extra hypothesis.
    98	
    99	The declaration is present but its proof remains open.  Issue~\#19 owns the
   100	Stage~4.2 statement and this discrepancy record; \ghissue{47} owns the
   101	Stage~4.3 proof from the product form and generalized Pauli commutation.
   102	
   103	This correction changes neither the definition of the extracted observables
   104	nor the source-faithful consistency and extraction conclusions.  It repairs an
   105	auxiliary algebraic assertion that is independent of the robustness estimates.
   106	
   107	\section{Conclusion}
   108	
   109	The source's cross-basis commutation claim is false for general
   110	$\widetilde u$ and $\widetilde v$.  The correct relation retains the phase
   111	$(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'}(\widetilde u\cdot\widetilde v))}$.
   112	Because the later argument does not invoke the false dichotomy, this is a
   113	local correction rather than an additional hypothesis on the extraction
   114	theorem.

     5	/-! # State-dependent consistency and strategy closeness
     6	
     7	The definitions are the finite-dimensional forms of `def:consistency` and
     8	`def:strategy-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-237`,
     9	from `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-288`.
    10	-/
    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    15	
    16	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    17	
    18	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    20	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    24	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    25	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    27	      if a = b then 0 else
    28	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)
    30	
    31	/-- The quantitative relation in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    32	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    33	def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    34	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
    38	  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ
    39	
    40	/-- Unit-alphabet specialization of `def:povm-distance`, blueprint
    41	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    42	noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    45	  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ
    46	
    47	/-- The unit-alphabet operator distance equals its one-outcome family form from
    48	`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper
    49	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    50	theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    51	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    52	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    53	    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
    54	      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl
    55	
    56	/-- The strategy-distance relation `def:strategy-distance`. The two strategies'
    57	local Hilbert spaces are identified, and both measurement distances are
    58	evaluated on the first strategy's state. Blueprint
    59	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    60	structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
    61	  /-- Identification of Alice's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    62	  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
    63	  /-- Identification of Bob's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    64	  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
    65	  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
    66	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
    67	  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
    68	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
    69	      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
    70	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    71	  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
    72	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
    73	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))
    74	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    75	
    76	end MIPStarRE.QPBT
