1	import Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.SchwartzZippel
     2	import Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.CommRing
     3	import Mathlib.RingTheory.MvPolynomial.Basic
     4	
     5	/-!
     6	# Polynomial preliminaries
     7	
     8	Packages the paper's low-individual-degree polynomial class together
     9	with Schwartz-Zippel bounds as thin wrappers around Mathlib's existing
    10	multivariate polynomial theorems.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	* `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex`, Section 3 (Preliminaries)
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open Finset Fintype
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    22	
    23	open MvPolynomial
    24	
    25	/-- `\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}` from the paper's definition of low-individual-degree
    26	polynomials. This is Mathlib's `MvPolynomial.restrictDegree` submodule. -/
    27	noncomputable abbrev polyFunc (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (d : ℕ) :
    28	    Submodule K (MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) :=
    29	  MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin m) K d
    30	
    31	/-- If `p ∈ polyFunc m K d`, then `p.degreeOf i ≤ d` for every variable `i`. -/
    32	theorem degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
    33	    {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K} (hp : p ∈ polyFunc m K d) (i : Fin m) :
    34	    p.degreeOf i ≤ d :=
    35	  MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mpr fun s hs =>
    36	    (MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree (σ := Fin m) (R := K) p d).mp hp s hs i
    37	
    38	/-- Paper label `rem:individual-degree-convention`.
    39	
    40	Increasing the individual-degree bound enlarges the corresponding low-degree
    41	polynomial class. -/
    42	theorem polyFuncMonotone {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] :
    43	    polyFunc m K d ≤ polyFunc m K (d + 1) := by
    44	  intro p hp
    45	  rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree] at hp ⊢
    46	  intro s hs i
    47	  exact (hp s hs i).trans (Nat.le_succ d)
    48	
    49	/-- The uniform agreement probability of two polynomials on `K^m`, written as a
    50	finite cardinality ratio over `K^m`. -/
    51	noncomputable def polynomialAgreementProbability (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] [Fintype K]
    52	    [DecidableEq K] (g h : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : ℚ≥0 :=
    53	  #{x ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → K)) |
    54	      MvPolynomial.eval x g = MvPolynomial.eval x h} /
    55	    (Fintype.card K ^ m : ℚ≥0)
    56	
    57	/-- If every individual degree of `p` is at most `d`, then the total degree of
    58	`p` is at most `m * d`. -/
    59	theorem totalDegree_le_mul_of_degreeOf_le {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
    60	    {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K} (hdeg : ∀ i, p.degreeOf i ≤ d) :
    61	    p.totalDegree ≤ m * d := by
    62	  rw [MvPolynomial.totalDegree]
    63	  refine Finset.sup_le ?_
    64	  intro s hs
    65	  calc
    66	    s.sum (fun _ e => e) = ∑ i : Fin m, s i := by
    67	      rw [Finsupp.sum_fintype]
    68	      intro i
    69	      rfl
    70	    _ ≤ ∑ _i : Fin m, d := by
    71	      refine Finset.sum_le_sum ?_
    72	      intro i _
    73	      exact (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mp (hdeg i)) s hs
    74	    _ = m * d := by
    75	      simp [Fintype.card_fin]
    76	
    77	/-- If two polynomials on `K^m` have total degree at most `d`, then the uniform
    78	agreement probability is at most `d / |K|`. -/
    79	theorem schwartzZippel_totalDegree {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    80	    [DecidableEq K] {g h : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K} (hneq : g ≠ h)
    81	    (hg : g.totalDegree ≤ d) (hh : h.totalDegree ≤ d) :
    82	    polynomialAgreementProbability m K g h ≤ d / Fintype.card K := by
    83	  have hsub_ne : g - h ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hneq
    84	  have hsub_deg : (g - h).totalDegree ≤ d :=
    85	    (MvPolynomial.totalDegree_sub g h).trans (max_le hg hh)
    86	  unfold polynomialAgreementProbability
    87	  rw [show {x ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → K)) |
    88	        MvPolynomial.eval x g = MvPolynomial.eval x h} =
    89	      {x ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → K)) |
    90	        MvPolynomial.eval x (g - h) = 0} by
    91	        ext x
    92	        simp [MvPolynomial.eval_sub, sub_eq_zero]]
    93	  calc
    94	    #{x ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → K)) |
    95	        MvPolynomial.eval x (g - h) = 0} /
    96	        (Fintype.card K ^ m : ℚ≥0)
    97	      ≤ (g - h).totalDegree / Fintype.card K := by
    98	          simpa using
    99	            (MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree
   100	              (n := m) (p := g - h) hsub_ne (Finset.univ : Finset K))
   101	    _ ≤ d / Fintype.card K := by
   102	          gcongr
   103	
   104	/-- Schwartz-Zippel for the paper's low-individual-degree class
   105	`\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}`. -/
   106	theorem schwartzZippel_individualDegree {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   107	    [DecidableEq K] (g h : polyFunc m K d) (hneq : g ≠ h) :
   108	    polynomialAgreementProbability m K g.1 h.1 ≤ ((m * d : ℕ) : ℚ≥0) / Fintype.card K := by
   109	  have hval_ne : g.1 ≠ h.1 := by
   110	    intro hgh
   111	    apply hneq
   112	    exact Subtype.ext hgh
   113	  have hg_degOf : ∀ i, g.1.degreeOf i ≤ d :=
   114	    degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc g.property
   115	  have hh_degOf : ∀ i, h.1.degreeOf i ≤ d :=
   116	    degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc h.property
   117	  exact schwartzZippel_totalDegree (g := g.1) (h := h.1) hval_ne
   118	    (totalDegree_le_mul_of_degreeOf_le hg_degOf)
   119	    (totalDegree_le_mul_of_degreeOf_le hh_degOf)
   120	
   121	end MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

1415	 \subsection{Pulling the $X$ and $Z$ measurements apart}
  1416	\label{sec:separating}
  1417	
  1418	
  1419	Recall the decoding map of the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}. This map takes in a polynomial $g \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ and returns a string $\coded(g) \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$ consisting of the evaluations of $g$ on the points in the hypercube $\{0,1\}^m$.
  1420	We now use this decoding map to construct a new set of measurement operators out of $\hat{S}$.
  1421	First, we introduce some notation. For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and all degree $d$ polynomials $g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ define projectors
  1422	\[ \hat{S}^X_g = \sum_{g_\zpt} \hat{S}_{g,g_\zpt} \quad  \text{and}  \quad \hat{S}^Z_g = \sum_{g_\xpt} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g}\;,\]
  1423	where the measurement $\{\hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is given by \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}.
  1424	
  1425	For all $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$, and $a \in \F_q$, define the projector
  1426	\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tauwu}
  1427	 \tau^{W}_{a}(\tilde{u}) = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits} \,:\, h \cdot \tilde{u} = a} \tau^W_{h}
  1428	\end{equation}
  1429	where recall that $\tau^W_h$ is the projector corresponding to measuring $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$ in the $W$ basis and obtaining $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ as the outcome. For all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ define the projective measurement $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}_{a \in \F_q}$ by 
  1430		\begin{equation}
  1431		\label{eq:tilde_M}
  1432		\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a =  \sum_{g} \hat{S}^W_g \otimes \tau_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}^W(\tilde{u})\;.
  1433		\end{equation}
  1434		If $\hat{S}^W_g$ is viewed as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice'$ (resp. $\bob \bob'$) then we view $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ (resp. $\bob \bob' \bob''$). (When necessary we will indicate via subscripts which registers the operators are acting on.)
  1435	The $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ are projective because the $\hat{S}^W_g$ and $\tau^W$ operators are projective.
  1436	
  1437	
  1438		For all $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$ define the observable
  1439		\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tildewj}
  1440			\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) = \sum_a (-1)^{\tr(e_j a)} \, \tilde{M}_a^{W,\tilde{u}} \;,
  1441		\end{equation}
  1442		where $\{e_j\}_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}}$ denotes the self-dual basis for $\F_q$ over $\F_2$ specified in \Cref{sec:subfields}. Let $\tau^W$ be the generalized Pauli observable defined in Section~\ref{sec:generalized-pauli}. Observe that
  1443		\begin{align*}
  1444		\Big ( \sum_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \Big ) \otimes \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})
  1445		&= \sum_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \sum_h (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} (-1)^{\tr(e_j(\tilde{u} \cdot h))} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \otimes \tau^W_h\\
  1446		&= \sum_{g_W} \sum_a  (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\tilde{u} \cdot\coded(g_W) + a))} \hat{S}_{g_W}^W \otimes \Big( \sum_{h:\, h\cdot \tilde{u} = a}\tau^W_h\Big)\\
  1447			&= \sum_{g_W} \sum_a  (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\tilde{u} \cdot\coded(g_W) + a))} \hat{S}_{g_W}^W \otimes \tau^W_a(\tilde{u})\\
  1448			&= 		\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \;,
  1449		\end{align*}
  1450		where the first equality uses the definition of $\tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})$, the second uses the definition of $\hat{S}^W_{g_W}$ and regroups terms, the third uses the definition~\eqref{eq:def-tauwu} of $\tau^W_a(\tilde{u})$, and the last is by a change of variables. These equations in particular show that the observable $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ is Hermitian and squares to the identity, because the measurement $\{ \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$ is projective. 
  1451		Furthermore, it can be verified by direct calculation that the observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ satisfy the same relations as the generalized Pauli group. Specifically, for all $j,j' \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, $\tilde{u}, \tilde{v} \in \F_q^\nqubits$,
  1452		\[
  1453			\tilde{X}^j(\tilde{u}) \tilde{Z}^{j'}(\tilde{v}) = \begin{cases}
  1454			\tilde{Z}^{j'}(\tilde{v}) \tilde{X}^j(\tilde{u})  & \qquad j \neq j' \\
  1455			(-1)^{\tr((e_j \tilde{u}) \cdot (e_j \tilde{v}))} \tilde{Z}^{j}(\tilde{v}) \tilde{X}^j(\tilde{u}) & \qquad j = j'
  1456			\end{cases}~.
  1457		\]
  1458		The next lemma shows that the measurements $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}$  and observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$  are consistent with the original points measurements, and are self-consistent. 
  1459		
  1460	
  1461	
  1462

1458		The next lemma shows that the measurements $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}$  and observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$  are consistent with the original points measurements, and are self-consistent. 
  1459		
  1460	
  1461

  1463	\begin{lemma}
  1464	  \label{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}
  1465	Let $\delta_S$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}.
  1466	For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ and $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, the measurements $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}_{a \in \F_q}$ and observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ satisfy the following properties:
  1467	\begin{enumerate}
  1468	\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, for all $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, and on average over uniformly random $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1469		\[
  1470			\Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \simeq_{\delta_S} M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''}
  1471		\]
  1472		and
  1473		\[
  1474			\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \;.
  1475		\]	
  1476		\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) On average over uniformly random $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$,
  1477		\[
  1478			\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \approx_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})\,.
  1479		\]
  1480	\end{enumerate}
  1481	\end{lemma}
  1482	
  1483	\begin{proof}
  1484	We show the first item of the lemma for the case when $M^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ acts on register $\alice$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ acts on registers $\bob \bob' \bob''$ (the argument for when the $\alice$ and $\bob$ registers are interchanged proceeds analogously):
  1485		\begin{align*}
  1486			&\E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_a \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1487			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g,a} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (M^{(\Point,W),u}_a)_{\alice} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u) -a}(\ind_m(u)))_{\bob''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1488			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u)})_{\alice \bob''} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1489			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)})_{\alice \bob''} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1490			&\geq 1 - \delta_S\;.
  1491		\end{align*}
  1492		The second line follows from expanding the definition of $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ using~\eqref{eq:tilde_M}, the third line follows from the definition of $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ given in Section~\ref{sec:expanding}, the fourth line follows from the fact that $\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u) = g(u)$, and the fifth line follows from \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}. This implies the first item of the Lemma.
  1493	
  1494	
  1495	To show the second item we first argue that, on average over $\tilde{u}$, 
  1496		\begin{equation}
  1497			\label{eq:qld-pulling-cons}
  1498			\Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \approx_{\delta_S} \Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\bob \bob' \bob''}.
  1499		\end{equation}
  1500		This follows because on average over $u \in \F_q^m$ and $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ we have
  1501		\begin{align}
  1502			&\Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \label{eq:qld-pulling-0} \\
  1503			\approx_{\delta_S}& \Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\alice \alice'\alice''} \cdot \Big ( \sum_g (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes  (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)})_{\bob \alice''} \Big) \label{eq:qld-pulling-1} \\
  1504			=_{\phantom{\delta_S}}& \sum_g \Big ( (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}(\tilde{u}))_{\alice''} \Big) \cdot \Big(\sum_{r,s: r + s = g(u)} (M^{(\Point,W),u}_r)_{\bob} \otimes (\tau_s^W(\ind_m(u)))_{\alice''} \Big) \label{eq:qld-pulling-2} \\
  1505			=_{\phantom{\delta_S}}& \sum_{\substack{g,h: \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}}  (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \otimes (M^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h)(u)})_{\bob}~. \label{eq:qld-pulling-2b}
  1506		\end{align}
  1507		The first inequality follows from right-multiplying~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-0} by the approximation~\eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons} in \Cref{lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper} (to be proved below) and using Fact~\ref{fact:add-a-proj}. Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-2} follows from expanding the definition of $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$.  To obtain Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-2b}, we expanded the definitions of $\tau^W_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}(\tilde{u})$ and $\tau^W_s(\ind_m(u))$ using~\cref{eq:def-tauwu}, and the fact that $h \cdot \ind_m(u) = g_h(u)$ (due to \cref{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}). Thus for all $g \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ and $s \in \F_q$ we have
  1508		\[
  1509			\tau^W_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}(\tilde{u}) \cdot \tau^W_s(\ind_m(u)) = \sum_{\substack{h: \\ (\coded(g) - h) \cdot \tilde{u} = a \\ g_h(u) = s}} \tau^W_h~.
  1510		\]
  1511	
  1512

  1765	which implies that 
  1766	\[
  1767		\bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S} \;.
  1768	\]
  1769	Define the unnormalized state $\ket{\aux_0}$ on the registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ as
  1770	\[
  1771		\ket{\aux_0}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} = (\bra{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''} \cdot \ket{\vartheta}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''}
  1772	\]
  1773	and define the normalized state $\ket{\aux} = \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \ket{\aux_0}$. 
  1774	The inner product between $\ket{\vartheta}$ and $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$ can thus be evaluated as
  1775	\begin{align*}
  1776		\bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) &= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux_0} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) \\
  1777		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1778		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|^2 \\
  1779		&= \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \| \\
  1780		&\geq \sqrt{1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S}} \\
  1781		&\geq 1 - O(\sqrt{\delta_S})\;.
  1782	\end{align*}
  1783	This implies $\| \ket{\vartheta} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, which establishes the first item of the lemma.
  1784	
  1785	We now establish the second item of the lemma. In what follows, all $\simeq$ and $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$. From \Cref{lem:qld-win-implications} we have the following implications: for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1786		\begin{align}
  1787		\label{eq:qld-unitary-2}
  1788		M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} &\simeq_\eps \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a\;, \\
  1789		\label{eq:qld-unitary-3}
  1790		\Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a &\simeq_\eps  M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''}\;,
  1791		\end{align}
  1792		where $M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h$. 
  1793	From \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that
  1794		\begin{equation}
  1795		\label{eq:qld-unitary-4}
  1796			M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;.
  1797		\end{equation}
  1798	Using \Cref{fact:triangle-for-simeq} with Equations \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-2}, \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-3}, and \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-4}, we get 
  1799		\begin{equation}
  1800			\label{eq:qld-unitary-5}
  1801			M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_S}} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;,
  1802		\end{equation}
  1803		where we used that $\delta_S \geq \eps$. 
  1804		
  1805		Next, we have for all $u \in \F_q^m$ 
  1806		\begin{align}
  1807			&V_\bob \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \notag \\
  1808			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))    \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1809			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_h   \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1810			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1811		= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1812	= &\Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''}\;,		\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}
  1813		\end{align}
  1814		where in the second line we expanded out the definitions of $V_\bob$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ (defined in \cref{eq:tilde_M}); in the third line we expanded out the definition of $\tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))$ (defined in \cref{eq:def-tauwu}) and used the fact that for all $h \in \F_q^M$, the inner product $h \cdot \ind_m(u)$ is equal to $g_h(u)$; in the fourth line we used the identities
  1815		\[
  1816			\tau^X(s) \tau^Z_h \tau^X(s)^\dagger = \tau^Z_{h + s} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \tau^Z(s) \tau^X_h \tau^Z(s)^\dagger = \tau^X_{h + s}~;
  1817		\]
  1818		and in the fifth line is due to the following short calculation: for all fixed $g_W$ we have
  1819		\begin{align*}
  1820			\sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a}  \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) - g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) + g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h': g_{h'}(u) = a} \tau^W_{h'}~.
  1821		\end{align*}
  1822		The second equality from the fact that $\F_q$ is a field of characteristic $2$ (so subtraction is the same as addition), and the third equality follows from the fact that letting $h' = h + \coded(g_W)$, we have $g_{h'} = g_h + g_W$ (in other words, the low-degree encoding $h \mapsto g_h$ is linear in $h$). 
  1823		
  1824		
  1825	
  1826	
  1827	Let $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. We show that $V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}$ (the argument for the operators acting on registers $\bob \bob' \bob''$ proceeds identically). 
  1828		\begin{align}
  1829			&\sum_h \bra{\Delta} \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}  \right)^\dagger \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \right) \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1830			&= 2 - 2 \Re \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice\, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1831			&= 2 - 2 \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-7}
  1832	\end{align}
  1833		where in the last line we used that $(\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} = (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1834		We now claim that
  1835		\begin{align}
  1836		&  \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \notag \\
  1837		&\approx_{md/q}  \E_u \sum_{\substack{h, h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-8} \\
  1838		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1839		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes V_\bob  \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-9}
  1840		\end{align}
  1841		where the equality in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9} follows from the identity in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-6}, and the approximation in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-8} follows from the following calculation:
  1842		\begin{align*}
  1843			& \E_u \sum_{\substack{h \neq h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \\
  1844			&= \sum_{h \neq h'} \left( \E_u \mathbf{1}[g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)] \right) \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \\
  1845			&\leq \frac{md}{q}\;.
  1846		\end{align*}
  1847		In the last line we used that for for distinct $h \neq h'$, the polynomials $g_h \neq g_{h'}$ and thus by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma can only agree on at most $md/q$ fraction of points $u \in \F_q^m$. 
  1848		
  1849		Continuing from \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}, we use the first item of the Lemma which shows that $\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$ and equivalently $\| V_\alice^\dagger \otimes V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\hat{\psi}} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, so 
  1850		\begin{align*}
  1851			\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}} &\approx_{O(\delta_S^{1/4})} \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1852			&\geq 1 - O(\delta_S^{1/2})\;,
  1853		\end{align*}
  1854	        where the last line comes from \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-5}.
  1855		Together with \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}, 
  1856		\[
  1857		\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}} \leq O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)\;.	
  1858		\]
  1859		This concludes the proof of the second item of the lemma.
  1860	\end{proof}
  1861	
  1862	We now prove \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}.
